info.name: Programs resource (local)
info.description: Tests the Programs resource: create, list, get, update, delete, undelete, the module manifest, what the admin builds on a leaf (a rule or typed settings, including library-backed ones), and the error cases. Needs the HTTP server on {{base_url}} (default http://localhost:8090) and, for the library settings, global-settings running with a library whose id is in {{library_id}}. Run top to bottom; each folder deletes its own test program.

item.name: Programs
item.description: Run top to bottom. A fresh slug is generated on the first run; 'Reset' clears it.

request.description: One transaction: program + picked modules (with ancestors) + Overview + counters + audit + outbox.

exec: pm.test('premade modules carry handler and api_base', () => { const a = b.modules.find(m => m.key === 'enrollment.applications_approvals.application_panel'); pm.expect(a.source).to.eql('premade'); pm.expect(a.handler_key).to.eql('applications'); pm.expect(a.api_base).to.eql('applications'); });
pm.test('every module has source and api_base for premade', () => r.filter(m => m.source === 'premade').forEach(m => pm.expect(m.api_base).to.be.a('string')));
pm.test('mode is null until the admin chooses Rule or Settings', () => r.forEach(m => pm.expect(m.mode).to.eql(null)));

pm.test('deleted program listed with state DELETED', () => { const m = pm.response.json().results.find(r => r.id === pm.collectionVariables.get('program_id')); pm.expect(m.state).to.eql('DELETED'); });

item.name: Settings and rules
item.description: What the admin builds on a leaf: a RULE (the frontend renders the rule engine) or SETTINGS (a name and a type each: boolean = Yes/No, number, text, radio, checkbox, dropdown). Library-backed settings read their options from global-settings, so {{library_id}} must be a library that exists there. Run top to bottom; the last request deletes the test program.

item.name: 1. Create: a rule leaf + a settings leaf with every type

request.description: Pre Enrollment becomes a RULE leaf. Warranty becomes a SETTINGS leaf: boolean (Yes/No), number, text, radio with its own options, a dropdown fed ONLY by a global-settings library, and a dropdown with the admin's own values.

exec: pm.test('Pre Enrollment is a rule leaf (frontend renders the rule engine)', () => { pm.expect(pre.mode).to.eql('rule'); pm.expect(pre.rule).to.be.an('object'); pm.expect(pre).to.not.have.property('settings'); });
pm.test('Warranty is a settings leaf with 6 settings, in order', () => pm.expect(w.settings.map(s => s.name)).to.eql(['Warranty enabled','Max days','Notes','Grade','Coverage','Region']));

pm.test('each type says which control to draw', () => pm.expect([by['Warranty enabled'].render, by['Max days'].render, by['Notes'].render, by['Grade'].render, by['Coverage'].render]).to.eql(['yes_no','number_input','text_input','radio_group','dropdown']));

pm.test('defaults and required are kept', () => { pm.expect(by['Warranty enabled'].default).to.eql(true); pm.expect(by['Max days'].default).to.eql(90); pm.expect(by['Max days'].required).to.eql(true); pm.expect(by['Grade'].default).to.eql('a'); });
pm.test('manual radio: own options, source manual', () => { pm.expect(by['Grade'].options_source).to.eql('manual'); pm.expect(by['Grade'].options.map(o => o.code)).to.eql(['a','b','c']); });
pm.test('manual dropdown: explicit code kept, the other derived from the label', () => pm.expect(by['Region'].options.map(o => o.code)).to.eql(['north_america','eu']));

pm.test('library dropdown: the LIBRARY is the source of the options', () => { pm.expect(by['Coverage'].options_source).to.eql('library'); pm.expect(by['Coverage'].library_id).to.eql(pm.environment.get('library_id') || pm.collectionVariables.get('library_id')); pm.expect(by['Coverage'].library_error).to.eql(null); pm.expect(by['Coverage'].options.length).to.be.above(0); pm.expect(by['Coverage'].options.every(o => o.source === 'library')).to.eql(true); });

pm.test('boolean / number / text have no options and no source', () => ['Warranty enabled','Max days','Notes'].forEach(n => { pm.expect(by[n].options).to.eql([]); pm.expect(by[n].options_source).to.eql(null); }));

item.name: 2. Manifest: the same, read back (library options from memory)

exec: pm.test('settings come back with their options', () => { pm.expect(w.settings.length).to.eql(6); pm.expect(w.settings.find(s => s.name === 'Coverage').options.length).to.be.above(0); });
pm.test('only configurable leaves carry a mode', () => r.filter(m => m.mode).forEach(m => pm.expect(m.allow_components).to.eql(true)));
pm.test('under a few seconds even with a library', () => pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime).to.be.below(1000));
pm.test('manual options still there', () => pm.expect(w.settings.find(s => s.name === 'Grade').options.length).to.eql(3));

item.name: 3. PATCH: replace the settings (keep by id, add one, drop the rest)

request.description: An item with an id is kept and updated (same key, same saved values); one without is created; the ones not listed are removed. Options match by code: c is deactivated, d is added.

exec: pm.test('only the listed settings remain, in order', () => pm.expect(m.settings.map(s => s.name)).to.eql(['Warranty enabled (renamed)','Grade','Deductible']));

pm.test('the renamed one kept its id and key', () => { const s = m.settings[0]; pm.expect(s.id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('enabled_id')); pm.expect(s.key).to.eql('warranty_enabled'); pm.expect(s.default).to.eql(false); });
pm.test('options diffed by code: a, b kept, c gone, d added', () => pm.expect(m.settings[1].options.map(o => o.code)).to.eql(['a','b','d']));

item.name: 3b. PATCH without modules returns no manifest

exec: pm.test('renamed, no manifest, version unchanged by a rename', () => { pm.expect(b.name).to.eql('Postman Builder (renamed)'); pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property('modules'); });

item.name: 4. PATCH: settings -> rule while settings exist (400)

request.description: A leaf that holds something cannot silently become something else.

exec: pm.test('says to remove the settings first', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include('still has settings'));

item.name: 6. PATCH: now switch it to a rule

exec: pm.test('now a rule leaf', () => { pm.expect(m.mode).to.eql('rule'); pm.expect(m.rule).to.be.an('object'); pm.expect(m).to.not.have.property('settings'); });

item.name: 7. PATCH: back to settings, with a setting, in one request

request.description: A rule with no versions can be switched to settings.

exec: pm.test('settings leaf again', () => { pm.expect(m.mode).to.eql('settings'); pm.expect(m.settings.map(s => s.name)).to.eql(['Back again']); });
pm.test('listed again, disabled', () => { const m = pm.response.json().results.find(x => x.key === 'enrollment.stores.enrolled_stores_control_panel'); pm.expect(m.enabled).to.eql(false); });

item.name: 9. PATCH: add a new (premade) module, with a setting on it

exec: pm.test('the module and its ancestors were added', () => pm.expect(keys).to.include.members(['document_agreement','document_agreement.documents','document_agreement.documents.documents_panel']));
pm.test('a premade module can hold settings', () => pm.expect(m.settings[0].name).to.eql('Retention days'));

request.description: What global-settings sends when a library, attribute or option changes: our cached copy of the libraries is dropped and re-read, so the new option shows up on the next read. If a webhook secret is configured, add the header X-Webhook-Secret.
Soft-deletes the program this run created, so repeated runs leave nothing live behind.

item.name: Radio with nothing to pick from

exec: pm.test('message mentions library_id or at least one option', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("library_id or at least one option"));

item.name: Library AND own options (the library is the only source)

exec: pm.test('message mentions takes no options', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("takes no options"));

item.name: Library that does not exist in global-settings

exec: pm.test('message mentions does not exist in global-settings', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("does not exist in global-settings"));
pm.test('message mentions true or false', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("true or false"));

item.name: Default is not one of the options

exec: pm.test('message mentions not one of its options', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("not one of its options"));

item.name: Setting id that does not exist here

exec: pm.test('message mentions does not exist here', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("does not exist here"));

A typo in a field name is named (setting, not settings)
A module that is neither a key nor an object

exec: pm.test('message mentions a module must be a key', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include("a module must be a key"));
